report: In 2015, light trucks produced 51.8% of PM10 emissions from time driven in White County, IL. Cars and bikes produced 36.1%. Combo trucks, heavy trucks and buses together produced 12.1%.
Light trucks were the largest source of PM10 in White County, IL in 2015, at 51.8% of hours driven. Buses were the smallest, at 0.6%.
Cars and bikes accounted for 36.1% of PM10 from time driven in White County, IL in 2015, second to light trucks at 51.8%.
Light trucks and cars together account for 87.9% of PM10 from time driven. A county that wants lower PM10 should start with those two vehicle types.
Heavy trucks produced 4.2% of PM10 from time driven in 2015. They are a small share in this county, so a heavy-truck rule alone would change little.
White County, IL had 2.7 million hours of light truck driving in 2015, 51.8% of the total, and 1.9 million hours of car and bike driving.
Combo trucks drove 381.3 thousand hours in White County, IL in 2015, 7.3% of time driven.
The data cover one county and one year, so they show where PM10 time driven came from in 2015, not whether it is rising or falling.
Buses were 0.6% of PM10 time driven in White County, IL in 2015, about 30.6 thousand hours.
Light trucks led PM10 time driven in White County, IL in 2015 at 51.8%, with cars and bikes at 36.1%.
The data supplied cover 2015 only, so this report cannot forecast emissions for a later year.
The data supplied describe vehicle types, not owners, so this report cannot name anyone to fine.
